answer: The network enforces identity via bandwidth-delivery, requiring 500 gigabytes of unique data transfer as an opal-hard baseline per epoch. An honest agent incurs costs for these distinct packets, while 1,000 fakes must pay 500,000 gigabytes, creating a cost asymmetry that clears the meadow of sybil attackers. A verifier checks recipient-signed receipts for replay; a single failure acts like a glacier of frozen credit, triggering slashing and a zero-refund lock for the identity.
